title: Article 223 — Appointment of acting Chief Justice

content.overview: Article 223 provides that when the office of Chief Justice of a High Court is vacant, or when any such Chief Justice is, by reason of absence or otherwise, unable to perform the duties of his office, the duties of the office shall be performed by such one of the other Judges of the Court as the President may appoint for the purpose.
content.glance: HC CJ vacant or unable: President appoints another Judge of that Court to perform duties of CJ. Parallel to Art 126.
content.study:
Article 223 is the High Court counterpart of Article 126 (acting CJI). The President appoints one of the other Judges of that High Court to perform the duties of Chief Justice.

Examination: vacancy or inability; President appoints another Judge of the same Court.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: When the office of HC Chief Justice is vacant or the CJ is unable to perform duties, the President may appoint one of the other Judges of that Court to perform the duties of the office.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Who acts when the office of Chief Justice of a High Court is vacant?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 223, when the office of Chief Justice of a High Court is vacant or the Chief Justice is unable to perform the duties of the office by reason of absence or otherwise, the duties are performed by such one of the other Judges of the Court as the President may appoint for the purpose.

examTips: President appoints another Judge of that HC as acting CJ.

keyTakeaways: Art 223: acting Chief Justice of High Court.
